data.title: Metalite Expands Launay Property Along the Macamic Fault, Establishing Macamic-Authier Block as its Third Area of Gold Exploration
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Mapped Macamic Fault Segments Total Approximately 30 km; Three High-Quality Exploration Blocks Across the Launay Property

TORONTO, ON – TheNewswire – November 20, 2026 – Metalite Resources Inc. (CSE: METL) (OTC: JNCCF) (FSE: D680) ("Metalite" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the acquisition of additional mineral claims in Québec’s Launay district, expanding its northwestern exploration footprint along the Macamic Fault. The expansion encompasses 59 new claims and applications1 covering approximately 3,352 hectares and strengthens the Company’s position in the Macamic-Authier Block, one of three principal gold exploration areas being advanced at Launay.

The expansion follows Metalite’s fall 2026 exploration and ongoing historical-data compilation, which highlighted structural trends, geological contacts and preliminary responses warranting further investigation along the northwestern corridor.

"Our work this fall has given us a clearer basis for expanding Launay and deciding where to focus next," said Alex Storcheus, Executive Chairman of Metalite. "Macamic-Authier brings together an important stretch of the fault corridor, a historical silver-lead showing and a substantial body of exploration information that we can now examine as an integrated package. Together with the Chauvignet and Lyndhurst blocks, it gives us three distinct areas in which to test our geological ideas and build the next generation of exploration targets."

Three Blocks, a Shared Geological Framework

Metalite has organized its Launay exploration activities around three blocks. Their current mapped outlines cover approximately 14,000 hectares in total, with the following areas and principal features:

  • Chauvignet Block (~5,015 ha). This central exploration block includes the flagship Trojan Zone, where 105 diamond drill holes have been reported, totalling approximately 21,826 metres.2 The extensive historical exploration provides a foundation for understanding the gold-exploration setting along the Macamic structural corridor and for evaluating sheared volcanic rocks, intrusive contacts and quartz-vein systems in the district.

  • Macamic-Authier Block (~4,978 ha). The northwestern focus of the current expansion lies in the Macamic–Authier area, extending toward Taschereau. Its attraction combines the Macamic Fault corridor, the historical Chemin de Fer-Sud silver–lead showing, a substantial archive of geological and geophysical work, and practical road and nearby rail access. Parts of the mapped block remain subject to claim-application approval.

  • Lyndhurst Block (~3,933 ha). The southeastern block includes the interpreted intersection area of the Lyndhurst and Macamic structural corridors, an important focus for examining how faults, volcanic contacts and alteration relate to one another. The predecessor’s 2021 airborne magnetic and VLF-EM survey covered the Lyndhurst grid, providing data for structural interpretation and follow-up.

Click Image To View Full Size

Metalite’s GIS analysis of the regional SIGÉOM Macamic Fault trace identifies approximately 29.9 kilometres of mapped fault segments (shown in red on the accompanying map) within the three block outlines: ~7.9 km at Chauvignet; ~13.2 km at Macamic-Authier; and ~8.9 km at Lyndhurst. The Launay Property lies in the Abitibi Greenstone Belt, where volcanic rocks, intrusive contacts and major deformation zones provide the geological setting for the Company’s exploration strategy. Numerous historic gold showing have been identified in close proximity and adjacent to the faults and shears in the region, including the Macamic Fault. The Macamic structure is a regional northwest-trending sheared corridor. Historical work at Launay describes quartz–carbonate–tourmaline veining and sulphides in altered, sheared volcanic rocks associated with the fault system and its subsidiary structures. These relationships support investigating deformation, alteration and vein development together, rather than treating individual anomalies in isolation.

As reported on October 28, 2026, Metalite’s integrated program combined satellite imagery, radar, terrain analysis, historical geological information and prospecting, supported by TerraEye’s specialist spectral work. The program identified multiple geological follow-up localities, including potential bedrock exposures, structural and contact relationships, and preliminary spectral responses requiring ground verification.

This work, together with the continuing assessment of historical data, supported the decision to expand along the northwestern continuation of the Macamic structural corridor. The objective is to bring promising geological relationships into a coherent exploration program, with a view to evaluating the potential continuity of mineralization at a district scale.

Macamic-Authier Block: Bringing Historical Reports into a Modern Compilation

Metalite has identified, analysed and digitized 88 historical assessment reports whose mapped coverage overlaps the Macamic-Authier Block. The collection includes a significant body of geophysical information, together with geological mapping and drilling records. Bringing these sources into a common digital framework allows the Company to compare historical responses with mapped structures, mineral occurrences and the current claim configuration. Preliminary findings include:

  • Drilling. The compilation identifies 24 historical drill holes totalling approximately 3,606 metres directly within the Macamic-Authier Block3

  • Chemin de Fer-Sud: A Historical Mineralized Showing. A 1962 report4 by Québec resident geologist Jean Dugas describes three principal quartz veins in chloritic schist, with pyrite and minor chalcopyrite and galena; tourmaline and carbonate were also observed in one vein. A historical sample from one of the veins was reported to return 0.17 g/t Au, 77 g/t Ag, 0.12% Cu and 1.15% Pb (these historic assay results have not been verified in the field by Metalite professionals).

  • Road and Rail Access. The block benefits from road access in the Macamic-Authier-Taschereau area, with a railway within a few hundred metres of portions of the property.

  • Public Land Tenure. Metalite estimates that approximately half of the outlined block overlies public land.

Click Image To View Full Size

Historical logs and survey data are being digitized to identify what has been tested, where coverage is incomplete and which anomalies merit renewed examination. Metalite is also integrating historical geophysical and geochemical data to assess similarities and differences relative to the Trojan Zone and other areas of documented gold mineralization5.

Next Steps

Metalite continues to advance its comprehensive compilation and interpretation of historical geological, geophysical and drilling data across the Launay Property, integrating these datasets with the results of its 2026 exploration program to refine and prioritize prospective exploration targets. This ongoing work is being undertaken with a view to finalizing the Company's drill permit applications and advancing its most prospective areas toward drill testing. Metalite has been working closely with its geological and permitting consultants to complete the necessary technical documentation and regulatory submissions, with the objective of positioning the Company to undertake targeted drilling programs, subject to receipt of the required approvals and available funding.

About Metalite Resources Inc.

Metalite Resources Inc. is a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on the acquisition, exploration and advancement of precious-metals projects. The Company owns a 100% interest in the Arthurs Seat Silver-Antimony Project in New South Wales, Australia and a 100% interest in the Launay Gold Property, a district-scale gold project located in Québec's Abitibi Greenstone Belt. The Company's strategy is to create long-term shareholder value through the systematic exploration and advancement of high-potential mineral properties.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Carey Galeschuk, P.Geo., a "qualified person" as defined in NI 43-101. Mr. Galeschuk is an officer of Metalite and is not independent of the Company.

data.title: Danaher Teams Up With Microsoft To Develop AI-Powered Scientific Instruments, First Applications Expected This Year
data.description:
Key points:
  • The platform will use Microsoft Azure for secure cloud infrastructure and Microsoft Foundry to power AI agents for instrument control and insight generation.
  • The technology is designed to help scientists plan experiments, guide instrument operations, interpret results, and recommend corrective actions under human oversight.
  • In preliminary internal testing, novice scientists using an AI assistant with a Leica microscope took up to 83% less time and 68% fewer steps than those working without the assistant, Danaher said.

Healthcare company Danaher Corporation (DHR) announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft (MSFT) on Friday to develop smart, AI-powered scientific instruments and an interoperable platform designed to connect laboratory technologies and make research workflows more intelligent.

"With Microsoft, we are building a common foundation, so our instruments and laboratories work together consistently, as one connected Danaher," Danaher CEO Julie Sawyer Montgomery said.

At the time of writing in premarket trading, DHR shares traded marginally lower, while MSFT shares traded 2.3% lower.

What The Partnership Involves

The partnership will focus on developing a common agentic platform for instrument control and insight generation. It will use Microsoft Azure for secure, compliant cloud infrastructure and Microsoft Foundry to power AI agents that interpret results and guide instrument control.

The technology is being designed to help scientists translate scientific questions into experimental plans, configure instruments and methods, guide experiment execution, troubleshoot issues, and recommend next steps for review. Instrument hardware will operate within defined safety boundaries and under user oversight.

The first commercial applications are expected to reach Danaher customers in 2026. These include MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant, software from Danaher's Molecular Devices business for its high-content cellular imaging systems, designed to provide product support. Additional next-generation instruments using the platform are planned for 2027.

Danaher said the collaboration is part of its broader strategy to connect intelligence at scientific instruments with laboratory data, workflows and the execution of experiments. However, the company believes this could help scientists use experimental results to determine subsequent steps, supporting increasingly connected and autonomous research workflows under scientific oversight.

Early Testing Shows Potential Time Savings For Scientists

In preliminary internal testing, novice scientists conducting an AI-assisted experiment on a Leica microscope took up to 83% less time and up to 68% fewer steps to complete the experiment than novices working without the AI assistant, Danaher said. The company added that the participants produced high-quality data and completed the experiment in a time comparable to an expert.

Microsoft Executive Vice President and Chief Revenue Officer Deb Cupp said the partnership aims to give scientists more choice and control, while allowing them more time for discovery. She added that the collaboration aligns with Microsoft's goal of translating AI into real-world impact.

How Retail Views MSFT-DHR Partnership?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment toward DHR remained in the ‘Bullish’ territory, with ‘Normal’ message volumes; however, sentiment toward MSFT remained in the ‘Bearish’ territory over the past 24 hours.

DHR shares are marginally lower year-to-date, while Microsoft shares have gained approximately 3%.

data.title: Utz Brands, Inc. and Intersnack Group GmbH & Co. KG Announce Completion of Transaction to Take Utz Private
data.description:
Utz Brands, Inc. (NYSE:UTZ) (“UBI” or the “Company”), a leading U.S. manufacturer of branded salty snacks, and Intersnack Group GmbH & Co. KG (“Intersnack Group” or “Intersnack”), a leading, multinational savory snack manufacturer, today announced the completion of the previously announced transaction pursuant to which Intersnack Group acquired all outstanding shares of Class A Common Stock of UBI for $14.25 per share, a premium of approximately 91% to the unaffected closing price on July 20, 2026. The closing of the transaction follows approval by UBI stockholders at the Company’s Special Meeting of Stockholders on November 13, 2026. UBI’s Class A Common Stock has ceased trading on the New York Stock Exchange and will be officially delisted. Following the closing of the transaction, the Utz business will be held by Utz Brands Holdings, LLC (“Utz Brands Holdings”).

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119130284/en/

Utz Brands and Intersnack Group announce completion of the transaction to take Utz private.

This partnership between Intersnack Group and entities affiliated with Utz’s founding family marks a pivotal moment for Utz, maintaining Utz’s century-long history of family ownership while establishing Intersnack Group’s presence in the large and attractive U.S. snacking market. With Intersnack Group’s expertise in innovation and operations, Utz will be positioned to forge even stronger consumer relationships and support continued investment in its brands. Utz is well positioned to build on its strong foundation and deep U.S. market knowledge to accelerate long-term growth and create meaningful benefits for all of its stakeholders.

“Today marks the beginning of an important new chapter for Utz,” said Dylan Lissette, Executive Chairman of Utz Brands Holdings. “With affiliated entities of the Rice and Lissette Family and Intersnack Group as long-term owners, Utz has a committed ownership structure focused on preserving what makes the Company special while supporting its continued evolution. Intersnack’s experience and capabilities add meaningful depth and agility to our organization and will support our efforts to enhance our brands, improve our operations and pursue opportunities for sustainable growth. We are grateful to our associates, customers, suppliers and communities whose contributions have shaped Utz’s success.”

“The completion of our partnership with the Rice and Lissette family represents an important milestone for Intersnack,” said Johan van Winkel, Executive Chairman of Intersnack Group. “We share a long-term perspective and a strong belief in the potential of Utz’s brands and people. By bringing our complementary strengths together, we can support Utz’s next phase of growth while creating new opportunities for both partners.”

Advisors

Special Committee and Company:

Citi was lead financial advisor, serving as exclusive financial advisor to the Special Committee of the Board of Directors of Utz, and Sidley Austin LLP served as legal counsel to the Special Committee. RBC Capital Markets served as a financial advisor to Utz.

The Rice and Lissette Family:

Sageworth served as financial advisor to the Rice and Lissette Family, and Cozen O’Connor served as legal counsel to the Rice and Lissette Family.

Intersnack Group:

BofA Securities served as exclusive financial advisor to Intersnack Group and provided committed debt financing in support of the transaction. Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP served as legal counsel to Intersnack Group.

About Utz Brands, Inc.

Utz Brands, Inc. (NYSE:UTZ) manufactures a diverse portfolio of savory snacks through popular brands, including Utz®, On The Border® Chips & Dips, Zapp’s®, and Boulder Canyon®, among others. After over a century with a strong family heritage, Utz continues to have a passion for exciting and delighting consumers with delicious snack foods made from top-quality ingredients. Utz’s products are distributed nationally through grocery, mass merchandisers, club, convenience, drug, and other channels. Based in Hanover, Pennsylvania, Utz has multiple manufacturing facilities across the U.S. to serve its growing customer base. For more information, please visit www.utzsnacks.com or call 1-800-FORSNAX.

About Intersnack Group

With nearly 60 years’ experience, Intersnack Group is one of the leading snack manufacturers in Europe and Oceania. The Group has grown continuously in recent years, both organically and through acquisition, becoming a market leader in savoury snacks. It operates 44 production sites across Europe, Australia, New Zealand, employs around 14,500 people and generated sales of approximately €4.5 billion/$5.0 billion in 2025.

Intersnack is passionate about enriching lives with great tasting snacks. Its portfolio spans potato chips, nuts, baked snacks and specialties and includes many well-loved local and international brands such as funny-frisch, Chio, POM-BÄR, Estrella, Hula Hoops, Tyrrell’s, Vico, Griffin's and Whole Earth.

By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Retail sales in Canada rose for a second straight month in September as households spent more at gasoline stations.

Sales increased 0.8% from the previous month to a seasonally adjusted 75.31 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.51 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday.

The advance was slightly stronger than the data agency's preliminary estimate sales were up 0.7% for the month, following an upwardly revised 1.4% increase in August.

Core retail sales, which exclude gas stations and fuel vendors and motor vehicle and parts dealers, edged up 0.1% in September

Compared with a year earlier, overall sales were 7.5% higher.

The agency said an early tally of receipts indicate sales declined 1.5% in October. The figure was based on responses from 58.1% of the retailers surveyed and will be revised.

data.title: Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September — Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian shoppers look to have reined in their spending in October after higher prices at the pump drove an increase in retail sales in the month before.

The value of retail trade in the country increased 0.8% in September from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 75.31 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.51 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday. That was a tick stronger than the 0.7% advance economists expected and followed upwardly revised growth of 1.4% in August.

An early look at receipts indicates sales in October dropped 1.5%, which would be the sharpest fall since February 2025.

That estimate suggests a soft start to the final quarter of 2026. Households have so far weathered heightened trade and economic uncertainty and the shock of elevated energy costs, but the job market has struggled in recent months and the central bank in late October raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years.

Statistics Canada offered no detail with its October estimate, which was based on the responses of roughly 58% of retailers surveyed and will be revised.

The data agency's survey for showed sales in September were up in five of the nine industry segments it tracks, led by trade at gasoline stations and fuel vendors. Stripping out fuel, sales edged up 0.1 for the month.

In volume terms, sales overall were up a modest 0.1% in September and 3.4% above the level a year earlier.

Total sales for the third quarter increased 1.2%, softening from the prior quarter's 2.2% growth, though the volume of trade for the latest quarter was up 1% versus a softer 0.4% in the second quarter.

Consumer spending has remained solid this year, and is expected by the Bank of Canada to help underpin a recovery in economic growth in 2027. Still, there are concerns households will cut back on outlays the longer energy costs remain elevated.

The Bank of Canada's focus on rising inflation risk prompted it to raise its policy interest rate. Annual inflation has been at, or above, the upper end of the bank's 1%-3% control range four months running, holding at 3.1% in October even as underlying measures of core inflation have remained more contained.

The September retail data showed gas and fuel sales were up a second month in a row, increasing 6.9% in nominal terms and 1.6% on a volume basis.

Sales at motor vehicle and parts dealers also rose a second consecutive month, climbing 0.2% from the prior month thanks to growth at new core dealers.

Core sales, which strips out both fuel and autos, nudged up 0.1% for the month with a boost from general merchandise stores. Canadians also spent more on clothing, accessories, luggage and leather goods and on health and personal care in September.

The sharpest fall came from food and beverage sales, driven by weakness at supermarkets and other grocery retailers.

The Bank of Canada projects the economy will slow in the final quarter of 2026 as the country adjusts to the latest U.S. tariffs, then recover next year. An estimate of industry accounts suggests gross domestic product contracted 0.1% between August and September after essentially no change the previous two months.

At the same time, employment in Canada has fallen three months running, driving the jobless rate in October to a six-month high of 6.7%.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest single-day outflow since launching. The same session saw $727 million in crypto liquidations, with bullish traders absorbing most of the damage.

Institutional demand is weakening, leveraged buyers are being forced out, and the Federal Reserve’s increasingly hawkish outlook is making speculative assets less attractive.

Bitcoin is now approaching $60,000, a level that could determine if the correction finds a floor or develops into something uglier.Xrp (XRP)24h7d30d1yAll timeBitcoin ETF Exodus and $727M Liquidations Put Bulls on the Defensive

That demand is now moving in the opposite direction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.1 billion this week alone. November’s cumulative withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion.Bitcoin ETF Flows,

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

The next downside area sits around $58,000, while more aggressive technical projections point toward $53,700.

The daily chart offers little encouragement for bulls. Bitcoin trades below its major moving averages, while bearish momentum continues to dominate. A sustained recovery in ETF flows would become increasingly important to prevent further deterioration.

Scenario 2: Bitcoin stabilizes between $60K and $62K.BTC USD,

This would give buyers time to absorb available supply without immediately reversing the entire November decline.

The liquidation wave has already removed considerable leverage from the market. If ETF withdrawals begin slowing, Bitcoin could establish a trading range before attempting another recovery.

But sideways trading alone would not confirm a bottom. Buyers need to demonstrate that they can defend support through multiple sessions.

Scenario 3: Bitcoin reclaims $62K and launches a relief rally.BTC USD,

A recovery above $62,000 would provide the first meaningful sign that sellers are losing control. A move toward $65,000 would then become possible, followed by resistance around $68,000.

Consistent ETF inflows, improving market sentiment, and a weaker dollar would strengthen this scenario. Without those developments, any rebound risks becoming another opportunity for sellers to exit.Should Bitcoin Holders Sell, Hold or Buy the Dip?

For existing holders, the decision depends heavily on their entry price, investment horizon, and exposure. Long-term holders who bought substantially below current prices have more room to withstand volatility. Selling simply because Bitcoin crossed a psychological threshold risks locking in profits or losses without knowing whether the broader investment thesis has changed.

However, investors holding leveraged positions face a different problem. Falling prices can trigger forced liquidations regardless of their long-term convictions. Reducing leverage and protecting available capital should take priority over waiting for a rebound.

For buyers, the temptation to buy the dip is understandable. Bitcoin is considerably cheaper than it was just weeks ago, but cheaper does not automatically mean undervalued.

Buying in stages rather than committing an entire allocation around $61,000 offers more flexibility if the market tests $58,000 or even $53,700.

Bitcoin price remains vulnerable to another leg down. The $60,000 level is no longer just a psychological milestone. It is where the next major battle between buyers and sellers.
